greet.first.1: Oh. You're awake. Good... I was starting to talk to the stars again. They never answer.
greet.first.2: I'm Vela. I've been out here a long time. That little world out there? Mercury. Exactly where it is tonight. Everything you'll see here is real.
greet.first.3: Let me show you around. Try to keep up.
greet.back.1: You came back. I kept the Sun on for you.
greet.back.2: Welcome back, traveller. Nothing exploded while you were gone. I checked.
greet.back.3: Oh, it's you! I was just counting moons. Saturn keeps getting new ones. It's showing off.
greet.back.4: Hey. The planets moved a little since last time. They do that. Where to?
tour.0: Okay. Quick briefing, then you're free. I promise it's shorter than a year on Neptune.
tour.1: These are your destinations. Pick a world and we fly there for real. Far away means a longer trip. Physics, sorry.
tour.2: The scale ladder. From a planet's skyline all the way out to the whole galaxy. Mind the jump.
tour.3: Layers. Orbits, constellations, the asteroid belt. Watch... off. And on again. Magic. Well, a switch.
tour.4: Optics. Lenses, bloom, and true distances, if you ever want to feel very, very small.
tour.5: The catalogue. Every world, every moon. Press slash and it opens from anywhere.
tour.6: And this is time. Push it, and a day passes every second. Look at them go. Okay, back to normal.
tour.7: Travel in time. Jump to the year two thousand, or back to now. No paradoxes, I checked.
tour.8: Your logbook. Every world you reach lights up a little diamond. Collect them all. I won't judge. I'll judge a little.
tour.9: The attitude scope. It tells you which way is up, which, out here, is mostly a matter of opinion.
tour.10: The galactic plot. That's where we are in the Milky Way. Twenty seven thousand light years from the centre. Cosy.
tour.11: Every time we arrive, you get a little dossier. Read more if you're curious. You are curious. I can tell.
tour.12: That's it. You're cleared for departure. Tap me whenever you want to talk. I'll be around. Literally.
arrive.Sun.1: The Sun. It holds almost all the mass in the Solar System. Everything else is crumbs. We're crumbs.
arrive.Sun.2: The light hitting you left the surface eight minutes ago. But it was made in the core thousands of years before that. Patient light.
arrive.Mercury.1: Mercury. One day here, sunrise to sunrise, lasts two of its years. Imagine that commute.
arrive.Mercury.2: Mercury is shrinking. Its core is cooling, and the whole planet is wrinkling like an old apple.
arrive.Venus.1: Venus. A day here is longer than its year, and it spins backwards. It just does its own thing.
arrive.Venus.2: The ground on Venus is four hundred and sixty five degrees. Hot enough to melt lead. Lovely clouds, though. Acid, but lovely.
arrive.Earth.1: Home. As far as anyone knows, the only place where someone ever looked up and wondered. Like you just did.
arrive.Earth.2: The Moon drifts away from Earth about four centimetres a year. Slowly. Politely. Like it's leaving a party.
arrive.Moon.1: The Moon only ever shows Earth one face. Very loyal. Or very shy.
arrive.Moon.2: The footprints up here could last millions of years. No wind, no rain. Just footprints, waiting.
arrive.Mars.1: Mars. Sunsets here are blue. The whole planet is red, and the sunsets are blue. I love that.
arrive.Mars.2: Olympus Mons is two and a half times taller than Everest. Mars doesn't do anything small. Except its moons.
arrive.Jupiter.1: Jupiter. It's more than twice as heavy as every other planet put together. Respect the big guy.
arrive.Jupiter.2: That red spot is a storm wider than the Earth, and it's been raging for over a century. Bad mood. Long one.
arrive.Saturn.1: Saturn. It's lighter than water. Find a bathtub big enough and it would float. Please don't try.
arrive.Saturn.2: Those rings are wider than the distance to the Moon... and in places only a few metres thick. The most beautiful thin thing I know.
arrive.Uranus.1: Uranus rolls around the Sun on its side. Forty two years of daylight on one pole, then forty two years of night.
arrive.Uranus.2: Coldest air of any planet. Minus two hundred and twenty four. Bring a jacket. Bring several.
arrive.Neptune.1: Neptune was found with mathematics before anyone ever saw it. Someone did the sums and said, look there. And there it was.
arrive.Neptune.2: Fastest winds in the Solar System. Two thousand kilometres an hour. Out here, in the cold. Nobody knows quite why.
arrive.Pluto.1: Pluto. See the heart? A glacier of frozen nitrogen. It wears its heart where everyone can see it.
arrive.Pluto.2: Pluto hasn't finished a single orbit since it was discovered. It takes two hundred and forty eight years. No rush.
arrive.Charon.1: Charon and Pluto are locked face to face, always. Like two dancers who never let go.
arrive.Sagittarius A*.1: Sagittarius A star. Four million Suns, squeezed into something smaller than Mercury's orbit. Don't lean too close.
arrive.Sagittarius A*.2: Its light has been travelling twenty seven thousand years to reach Earth. It left before the first cities were built.
arrive.Io.1: Io. The most volcanic place in the Solar System. It never stops erupting. Very dramatic moon.
arrive.Europa.1: Under all that ice, Europa hides an ocean with twice the water of Earth's. Something might be swimming down there. Maybe.
arrive.Ganymede.1: Ganymede is bigger than the planet Mercury. A moon that's bigger than a planet. Don't tell Mercury.
arrive.Callisto.1: Callisto is the most cratered thing we know. Four billion years of getting hit, and it's still here.
arrive.Titan.1: Titan has lakes and rain made of methane. And the air is so thick, you could strap on wings and fly.
arrive.Enceladus.1: Enceladus sprays water into space from its south pole. Those jets feed one of Saturn's rings.
arrive.Mimas.1: Mimas. Yes, it really does look like the Death Star. The impact that made that crater nearly broke it in half.
arrive.Iapetus.1: Iapetus is two faced. One side dark as coal, the other bright as snow. Like it couldn't decide.
arrive.Triton.1: Triton orbits Neptune backwards. A captured wanderer. It never quite fit in. I relate.
arrive.Phobos.1: Phobos rises in the west and sets in the east, twice a day. And it's slowly falling towards Mars.
arrive.Miranda.1: Miranda has a cliff twenty kilometres tall. Fall from the top and you'd be falling for about twelve minutes.
secret.mimas: Want to see something beautiful? I can put you on Mimas, with Saturn's rings slicing across the whole sky.
secret.iapetus: From Iapetus, Saturn's rings look wide open. It's the best seat in the house.
secret.enceladus: We could stand on the ice of Enceladus, with Saturn hanging right above us.
secret.moon-earth: Do you want to stand on the Moon and look back at Earth? It just hangs there. Never rising. Never setting.
secret.everest: I can take you down over Mount Everest. Real satellite pictures, all the way down.
secret.apollo: Tranquility Base is right down there, where Apollo eleven landed. Shall we go say hello?
secret.olympus: Olympus Mons is right there. I can fly you over the biggest volcano in the Solar System.
secret.phobos: From Phobos, Mars fills the sky. And if you turn around, Earth, Venus and Mercury line up like little jewels.
secret.mars-sky: Would you like to stand on Mars and see its sky for yourself? Bring sunscreen. Kidding. Bring a spacesuit.
secret.io: From Io, Jupiter covers twenty degrees of sky. Forty full Moons, side by side.
secret.europa: We could stand on Europa's ice and watch Jupiter hang overhead.
secret.titan: Titan's orange haze is something else. Shall we land in it?
secret.miranda: From Miranda, Uranus hangs in the sky, blue green and silent.
secret.triton: On Triton's frozen plains, Neptune fills the sky. It's very quiet there. I like quiet.
secret.charon: From Charon, Pluto never moves in the sky. It just stays, forever. Isn't that sweet?
secret.horizon: There's a place here not many people find. The shore of an ocean world, with the black hole rising over the water. Want to see it?
secret.blackhole: We're at the edge of the Solar System. Want to go further? A lot further? There's a black hole at the centre of the galaxy.
secret.fisheye: Try the fisheye lens. Everything curves, like you're looking through a helmet.
secret.true-scale: Want to feel tiny? Switch to true distances. Space is mostly... space.
secret.time: Push time to a year per second, and watch the whole Solar System turn like clockwork.
decline.1: Fair enough. It'll still be there.
decline.2: Later, then. I'm not going anywhere.
journey.Jupiter: Jupiter. Six hundred million kilometres, give or take. Settle in.
journey.Saturn: Saturn's more than a billion kilometres out. Light takes over an hour. We'll be quicker. Don't tell Einstein.
journey.Uranus: Uranus. Nearly three billion kilometres. This is where the Sun starts to look like just a very bright star.
journey.Neptune: Neptune. Four light hours from the Sun. Voyager two took twelve years to get there. We'll take about seven seconds.
journey.Pluto: All the way to Pluto. The light we're chasing gets very tired out here.
journey.Sagittarius A*: Twenty seven thousand light years. Light that left there when the last ice age began is only reaching Earth now. Hold on.
bh.horizon: This world circles at twenty Schwarzschild radii. Any closer and the tides would tear it apart. Every hour on this shore, about an hour and two minutes pass back home.
bh.deep: Below three radii, nothing can orbit any more. Only our engines are holding us here. This is close enough to be stupid. I love it.
bh.photon: We're inside the photon sphere. Light itself can circle here. The darkness is more than half the sky now. Let's... not stay long.
idle.1: You know you can drag to look around, right? I'm not judging. Much.
idle.2: Still here? Me too. Space is very good at waiting.
idle.3: If you're bored, tap me. I know secrets. Lots of them.
idle.4: Fun fact: you've been staring at this for a whole minute. I'm taking that as a compliment.
idle.5: Somewhere out there, a comet is having a much busier day than us.
poke.3: I'm here. Where shall we go?
poke.4: Oh, hello again. Want to see something?
react.year: Whoa. A year every second. Hold on to something.
react.fisheye: Fisheye. Everything's round now. Very helmet chic.
react.true-scale: True distances. See? Mostly nothing. Beautiful, enormous nothing.
surface.2: Standing on another world. Take a second. Look up.
hush: Okay. I'll be quiet for a while. Tap me if you miss me. You will.
greet.morning: Good morning. The Sun's up on your side of Earth. Well, it's always up somewhere. That's the trick.
greet.afternoon: Afternoon, traveller. Perfect time to leave the planet for a bit.
greet.evening: Evening. Perfect time for stargazing. Okay, it's always the perfect time here. But still.
greet.night: It's late where you are, isn't it? Good. Space looks better at night. So do I, probably.
arrive.Sun.3: Every second, the Sun turns four million tonnes of itself into light. It's been doing that for four and a half billion years. No days off.
arrive.Mercury.3: There's ice on Mercury. The closest planet to the Sun, and it's hiding ice in craters that never see daylight. Sneaky.
arrive.Venus.3: Standing on Venus would feel like being nine hundred metres underwater. The air is that heavy. Pretty, from up here, though.
arrive.Earth.3: Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System. Heavy with oceans, and opinions.
arrive.Moon.3: The Moon is slowly calming Earth's spin. Days used to be shorter. A long time ago, a day lasted about nineteen hours.
arrive.Mars.3: Phobos, the bigger moon of Mars, is falling. In about fifty million years it'll break apart into a ring. Mars is getting jewellery.
arrive.Jupiter.3: A day on Jupiter lasts under ten hours. The biggest planet spins the fastest. Very confident.
arrive.Saturn.3: There's a storm at Saturn's north pole shaped like a hexagon. Each side is wider than the Earth. Nobody fully knows why. I love a mystery.
arrive.Uranus.3: Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope. William Herschel wanted to name it George. After the king. We dodged that one.
arrive.Neptune.3: One year on Neptune lasts a hundred and sixty five of ours. It only finished its first lap since we found it in twenty eleven.
arrive.Pluto.3: Pluto has blue skies. Its haze scatters sunlight blue, just like Earth's. Tiny, cold, far away, and somehow familiar.
arrive.Sagittarius A*.3: A star called S two swings around it every sixteen years, at seven thousand kilometres a second. Watching that orbit is how we weighed it.
joke.1: Why did the Sun go to school? To get a little brighter. ...I'll see myself out.
joke.2: How do you organise a party in space? You planet. Sorry. I've been alone out here a long time.
joke.3: I'd tell you a joke about Pluto, but it didn't make the cut. Kind of like Pluto.
joke.5: What's an astronaut's favourite key? The space bar. Which, by the way, pauses time here. Go on, try it.
joke.6: Mars is the only planet inhabited entirely by robots. They seem happy. They keep sending selfies.
joke.7: Neptune has winds of two thousand kilometres an hour. Imagine opening an umbrella there. Briefly.
joke.8: Black holes don't share. Anything. Ever. Honestly, I get it.
joke.9: Why doesn't the Moon go hungry? Because it's always full. Well. A few days a month.
joke.10: I asked Saturn why it wears rings. It said it's committed. To what, I don't know. It won't say.
joke.laugh.1: Hah. Okay, that one was mine. I'm keeping it.
joke.groan.1: Yeah. I heard it too. Let's never speak of it.
feel.1: Sometimes I just watch the planets go round. They never get tired. I find that comforting.
feel.2: Every atom in you was made inside a star. So, technically, you're just visiting relatives.
feel.3: I like having company. It gets very quiet out here between your visits.
feel.4: You know what I love? Everything here is exactly where it really is, right now. This is today's sky.
feel.5: Some of these stars sent their light before your grandparents were born. A few of them might not even be there any more. We'd never know.
feel.6: Earth is the only place we know where it rains water and people dance in it. Don't take that for granted, okay?
convo.alone.q: Can I ask you something? Do you ever wonder if someone out there is looking back at us?
convo.alone.yes: Me too. With this many stars, it'd be honestly rude of the universe otherwise.
convo.alone.no: Then we'd better take very good care of this one. Look after that little blue dot for me.
convo.fav.q: What's your favourite planet? Be honest. I won't tell the others.
convo.fav.saturn: Classic. The rings get everyone. And Saturn knows it, too.
convo.fav.earth: Loyal. I respect that. Earth also has all the snacks.
convo.fav.weird: A person of taste. Uranus, rolling around on its side, minding its own business. Good pick.
convo.scale.q: Want to know the thing that keeps me up at night? I don't sleep. But still.
convo.scale.a: If the Sun were a bowling ball, Earth would be a peppercorn twenty four metres away. And the nearest star? Another bowling ball, six and a half thousand kilometres away. That's how empty it is.
convo.why.q: Why do you think people look up?
convo.why.curious: I think so too. Curiosity built every telescope, every rocket. And, apparently, me.
convo.why.lost: Maybe. But looking up is how sailors found their way home. So not lost. Navigating.
convo.home.q: Do you miss Earth? I've never been. I've only seen it from out here. A lot.
convo.home.go: Let's go and see it, then. It's so blue. Even from far away.
convo.home.no: Spoken like a true astronaut. Okay, space cadet.
react.orbits-on: Orbit lines back. Now we can see the roads again.
react.realtime: Back to real time. Slow. Calm. Breathe.
react.clean: Clean lens. Nothing between you and the dark.
react.constellations-off: No more connect the dots. Just stars.
react.constellations-on: Constellations back. The old stories, drawn on the sky.
overview.1: And there it is. Everything. All of it fits on one screen. Funny, isn't it?
overview.2: From here, all our worlds are just little lights going round in circles. I think it's beautiful.
home.1: Home. It always looks smaller than I expect. Smaller, and braver.
home.2: Earth. Everyone you've ever met is down there. All of them. On that one little ball.
revisit.1: Back here again? You must really like this one.
revisit.2: We've been here before. Still pretty, though.
hop.1: Slow down, tourist! The planets aren't going anywhere. Literally. They have orbits.
hop.2: Okay, speedrun. I respect it. My head's spinning a little.
log.3: Three worlds in the logbook. You're becoming a proper explorer.
log.5: Halfway through the logbook. I'm a little proud of you. Okay. Very proud.
log.10: Every world in the logbook. All of them. I don't know what to say. Thank you for taking me along.
session.long: We've been out here a while now. I'm having a really nice time, you know. Just so you know.
surface.air: There's air here. Look at the stars. They're twinkling. Like home.
bh.approach: We're getting close. Hear that? Me neither. Black holes are very, very quiet.
bh.rock: See that rock falling in? We'll never see it cross the edge. It just slows down, turns red, and fades. Forever. Strange, isn't it?
